chordInfo.name: Major Chords
chordInfo.subtitle: Master the foundation of Western harmony with major chords - the bright, stable, and joyful building blocks of countless songs.

fundamentals.label: Definition
fundamentals.value: A three-note consonant triad constructed by stacking a major third and a minor third above a root pitch.

fundamentals.label: Formula
fundamentals.value: Root + Major 3rd (4 semitones) + Perfect 5th (7 semitones). The major third provides the distinctive bright tonal color.

fundamentals.label: Interval Pattern
fundamentals.value: 4 semitones from root to third, followed by 3 semitones from third to fifth, creating pure acoustic consonance.

fundamentals.label: Sound Quality
fundamentals.value: Characterized by open acoustic stability and brightness, serving as the foundational reference point for Western harmony.

fundamentals.label: Harmonic Function
fundamentals.value: Acts primarily as the home tonic (I), stabilizing resolution point, or as the energetic dominant (V) and subdominant (IV) in tonal chord progressions.

applications.label: Pop & Rock
applications.value: Forms the backbone of iconic four-chord progressions (like I–V–vi–IV), providing accessible and memorable harmonic hooks.

applications.label: Folk & Country
applications.value: Drives traditional three-chord (I–IV–V) song structures with open cowboy chords that maximize natural acoustic string resonance.

applications.label: Classical & Film
applications.value: Serves as primary cadential resolution points (V–I authentic cadence) to deliver emotional closure and dramatic stability.

applications.label: Blues & R&B
applications.value: Provides the foundational triad beneath dominant seventh chords and extended voicings across standard 12-bar blues forms.

boxes.title: C Major Triad Construction
items: Root: C (1st scale degree establishing the tonal home base)
Major 3rd: E (3rd scale degree, 4 semitones above root, defining the chord's major tonality)
Perfect 5th: G (5th scale degree, 7 semitones above root, adding acoustic fullness and stability)
Interval Stacking: Root to Major 3rd (4 semitones) plus Major 3rd to Perfect 5th (3 semitones)
Acoustic Result: Balanced triad with minimal harmonic dissonance that rings clear across open strings

boxes.title: Harmonic Stability
items: Major 3rd Interval: Distinctive interval that triggers bright, consonant auditory perception
Perfect 5th Interval: Strongly reinforced overtone that anchors pitch center stability
Consonant Nature: Minimal internal frequency clashing allows chords to ring out cleanly without distortion
Tonal Home: Serves as the ultimate resting place in major key cadences (V to I)
Emotional Color: Uplifting, triumphant, or serene atmosphere depending on tempo and dynamics

boxes.title: Diatonic Relationship
items: Diatonic Position: Naturally occurs on scale degrees I, IV, and V in any major key
Major Keys: The three primary major chords in C major are C (I), F (IV), and G (V)
Primary Cadences: The movement from V (dominant) to I (tonic) forms the strongest harmonic resolution in Western music
Tonal Direction: Provides clear tension and release when paired with minor secondary chords (ii, iii, vi)
CAGED System: Moveable shapes allow major triads to be voiced across all five fretboard positions

voicingGroups.title: Moveable Major Chord Forms
voicingGroups.tipDescription: These moveable forms allow you to play major chords anywhere on the neck.

voicings.name: E-Shape Barre (6th string root)
voicings.notes: Based on open E major shape
voicings.use: Moveable up and down the neck

voicings.name: A-Shape Barre (5th string root)
voicings.notes: Based on open A major shape
voicings.use: Moveable up and down the neck

items.title: Pop Progression I-V-vi-IV
items.description: The most popular progression in modern music - used in thousands of songs from "Let It Be" to "Don't Stop Believin'"

items.title: Three-Chord Song I-IV-V
items.description: Foundation of folk and country music - simple yet powerful progression in "Blowin' in the Wind" and "Ring of Fire"

items.title: 50s Doo-Wop I-vi-IV-V
items.description: Classic 1950s progression with smooth circular motion - heard in "Stand By Me" and countless doo-wop classics

items.title: Emotional vi-IV-I-V
items.description: Starts minor and resolves to major - creates emotional journey from sadness to hope in "Hallelujah" and "Country Roads"

techniqueItems: Focus on clean major third intervals
applicationItems: Perfect for sing-alongs and campfire songs

practiceExercises.tipDescription: These exercises will help you master major chords and their applications.

exercises.title: Exercise 1: Open Chord Changes
exercises.content: Progression: C - G - D - A - E - F
exercises.detail: Practice clean transitions between all open major chords
exercises.tip: Start slowly, focus on finger placement and timing

exercises.title: Exercise 2: I-IV-V in Different Keys
exercises.tip: Essential for country, folk, and rock songs

exercises.title: Exercise 3: Pop Progression Mastery
exercises.tip: Learn the most popular progression in modern music

concepts.title: Chord Inversions
items: Root Position: C-E-G (root in bass)
First Inversion: E-G-C (3rd in bass)
Second Inversion: G-C-E (5th in bass)
Voice Leading: Smoother progressions
Bass Lines: More interesting movement

concepts.title: Chord Extensions
items: Add9: Major chord + 9th (Cadd9)
6th Chords: Major chord + 6th (C6)
Major 7th: Major chord + 7th (CMaj7)
Sus Chords: Suspended 2nd or 4th
Color Tones: Added harmonic richness
